To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TLR3 agonist poly(I:C) rapidly and lastingly alters glutamatergic function in the nucleus accumbens and increases the self-administration of ethanol.

(i) TLR3 activation induces a lasting increase in glutamate levels, (ii) the increase is associated with a decrease in the expression of glutamate transporters in the nucleus accumbens (NAcc), (iii) TLR3‐induced glutamate release is associated with an increase in the expression of genes involved in glutamate signaling, and (iv) TLR3 agonist administration enhances the reinforcing properties of ethanol.
